## jobs/convert

A document's text turned into Markdown by a model, a section
at a time, along a tree decided first.

`jobs/sections.js` settles the headings and cuts the text into requests,
each with its headings written in. A model converts a request — tables,
paragraphs, lists — and hands the headings back as they were given; what
it changes of them is put back, a heading it adds at a level it may not
use becomes a bold line, and one it loses sends the request back as two
halves. The answers are joined, a table cut by a split made whole again,
and an index of links goes on top.

Everything here is pure but the step that asks the model, which takes
the asking as a function. The job runner supplies it in the app; the
harness supplies its own.

## HEADING

## conversionMessages

The messages that ask a model to convert one request.

### Parameters

- `args` **[Object][430]**&#x20;
  - `args.title` **[string][429]** The document's title, for the model's bearings
  - `args.text` **[string][429]** The request's text, headings written in
  - `args.above` **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>** The headings the text sits under
  - `args.continued` **[boolean][432]** Whether the text goes on from a section begun before it

Returns **[Array][431]<{role: [string][429], content: [string][429]}>**&#x20;

## wordCount

How many words of running text a stretch has: letters only, so a table's
pipes and a page's numbers count for nothing on either side.

### Parameters

- `text` **[string][429]**&#x20;

Returns **[number][428]**&#x20;

## withoutRepeats

A text with any passage it gives twice kept once. Some PDFs give the
same passage twice — a sidebar drawn in two layers — and a model that
writes it once has dropped nothing; its words are counted against the
text's once. Only a run of lines repeated together counts: stat blocks
that share a line or two word for word are not a passage given twice.

### Parameters

- `text` **[string][429]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][429]**&#x20;

## firstAt

Type: [Map][433]<[string][429], [number][428]>

## REPEATED_RUN

How many lines in a row have to repeat an earlier run to be a passage given twice.

Type: [number][428]

## editDistance

How many single-character edits turn one string into another.

### Parameters

- `a` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `b` **[string][429]**&#x20;

## headingMatch

How a heading the model wrote stands to one it was given: the same
words, near enough the same — a letter the text had wrong, put right, as
a PDF that reads `ti` as `8` gives `Rou8nes` — or not the same heading.

### Parameters

- `written` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `given` **[string][429]**&#x20;

Returns **(`"same"` | `"near"` | null)**&#x20;

## asRead

Text as it was read, made safe to put under its headings: a line of it
that starts with `#` — a comment in a code listing — is not a heading,
and is escaped so that no reader takes it for one. The given headings,
written in as Markdown, are left as they are.

### Parameters

- `text` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `given` **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>**&#x20;

Returns **[string][429]**&#x20;

## fixHeadings

Put an answer's headings right. Each given heading is found in order —
as a heading at any level, or as a bold line the model demoted it to, in
the same words or near enough — and written back at the level it was
given, exactly as given unless the model put a misread letter right. A heading the
model added is kept only below the given heading it falls under; above
that, or before any given heading where none may go, it becomes a bold
line, since the tree is not the model's to change.

A given heading with nothing under it — one that groups the headings
after it — is easy for a model to drop; when it is, it is written back in
before the next one.

### Parameters

- `markdown` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `given` **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>**&#x20;
- `floor` **[number][428]** The level an added heading must be below: 6,
  where nothing may be added, as a conversion has it; lower lets a model
  add headings under the given ones
- `empty` **[Array][431]<[boolean][432]>?** For each given heading, whether it has no text of its own (optional, default `[]`)

Returns **{markdown: [string][429], missing: [Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>}**&#x20;

## checkConversion

Whether an answer is a conversion of its request, and if not, why not:
cut off, empty, missing a heading it was given, or far from the text's
length in words — shorter is text dropped or summarised, longer is text
made up.

### Parameters

- `args` **[Object][430]**&#x20;
  - `args.text` **[string][429]** What was sent
  - `args.markdown` **[string][429]** The answer, headings put right
  - `args.missing` **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>** Given headings the answer lacks
  - `args.finishReason` **([string][429] | null)?**&#x20;

Returns **([string][429] | null)** What is wrong, or null when nothing is

## cellsOf

The columns of a table row.

### Parameters

- `row` **[string][429]**&#x20;

## joinConverted

Two converted pieces as one. Where the first ends in a table and the
second, a continued part of the same section, opens with a table of as
many columns, they are one table cut by the split: the second's header
row goes if it repeats the first's, and becomes a row if it does not —
a model given a table's middle makes its first row the header.

### Parameters

- `first` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `second` **[string][429]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][429]**&#x20;

## splitRequest

Two halves of a request, for asking again. A request of several units is
cut between them; a request of one is cut inside it, at a paragraph near
its middle. Null when there is nothing to cut.

### Parameters

- `lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;
- `request` **[Request][320]**&#x20;

Returns **(\[[Request][320], [Request][320]] | null)**&#x20;

## convertRequest

Convert one request: ask, put the headings right, check, and — when the
check fails — ask again as two halves, twice over at most.

### Parameters

- `args` **[Object][430]**&#x20;
  - `args.title` **[string][429]**&#x20;
  - `args.lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;
  - `args.headings` **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>**&#x20;
  - `args.request` **[Request][320]**&#x20;
  - `args.ask` &#x20;
  - `args.note` &#x20;

- `depth` **[number][428]?** How many times this request has been halved already (optional, default `0`)

The converted document: the answers joined in order, and an index of

## jobs/explore

What a project holds, described for the model.

The model finds its way around a project by the listing, and a listing of
titles says little: "Notes 3", a paper by its file name. Explore gives each
document and folder a digest (`Digest` in types/models.js): a line for the
listing and a paragraph for when the model looks closer. It does it without
tools. The app knows what is in a folder, so it walks the tree itself and
sends each piece's text with a prompt, and a small model that can't be
trusted to call tools can still say what it read.

How the work is cut follows from how much text one request carries (the
budget, `budgetFor`):

- A folder whose text all fits is read whole, and the one answer describes
  it and each document in it long enough to be worth a line of its own. A
  lorebook of short entries is one request.
- Otherwise each document is read, small ones several to a request, and one
  longer than a request is read in parts along its headings, then put
  together from what was said of each part.
- A folder too big to read whole is put together from what was said of
  what it holds, its short documents as they are, in parts when they will
  not go in one request. The project's digest is put together last.

A document that holds others, as an import may make one, is described from
its own text when it has one, and what it holds beside it, each by itself;
one with no text of its own, a card's picture or an epub, is described from
what it holds, as a folder is.

A long section of a document (`SECTION_WORDS`) gets a line of its own, so
the model can tell which part of a long document to read: asked for in
the request that reads the section's heading, and kept on the document's
digest. Which sections is decided by how long they are, not by their
level: a book's chapters may be four headings down, and a rulebook's
one-sentence entries one.

Each request is a step of an `explore` job, waiting on the steps it reads
from (`after`), so documents are read side by side as far as the
connection allows. What is current is left alone: a digest says what it was
made from (`of`), and a document whose text has not changed, or a folder
nothing under it has changed in, keeps its digest.

Everything here is pure: the tree comes in as `ExploreNode`s, made from the
documents by whoever starts the job (`jobs/index.js`), and a step reads the
project as it stands when it runs through an `ExploreReader`.

## SECTION_WORDS

Type: [number][428]

## SECTION_WORDS

Type: [number][428]

## SECTION_WORDS

A section this long, its subsections with it, gets a line of its own on its
document's digest. Shorter, it is quicker to read than to describe.

Type: [number][428]

## ExploreNode

A document or folder as explore sees it.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `path` **[string][429]** As the tools give it: `Notes/Elara`, and `/` for the project
- `title` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `type` **(`"folder"` | `"text"` | `"file"`)**&#x20;
- `text` **[string][429]** What is read of it: a text's markdown, the text
  read out of a file; '' for a folder
- `words` **[number][428]**&#x20;
- `leftOut` **[string][429]?** Why it is not read, said in its folder's
  digest: `a codebase`, `a file with no text`
- `children` **[Array][431]<[ExploreNode][46]>** The ones shown to the model, in the outline's
  order: a folder's, or a document's that holds others
- `digest` **Digest?**&#x20;

## Piece

What a step puts together from: a digest made already, a short document's
text, an earlier step's answer, or something not read, by name.

Type: ({digest: [string][429]} | {text: [string][429]} | {step: [string][429]} | {left: [string][429]})

## ExploreWork

One request of an explore job.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `kind` **(`"read"` | `"part"` | `"gather"`)** Read documents whole, read part of
  one, or put together what was said of others
- `reads` **[Array][431]<[string][429]>?** read: the documents whose text it sends
- `whole` **[string][429]?** read: the folder read whole, when it is one
- `of` **[string][429]?** part: the document it reads part of; gather: the
  document or folder it puts together
- `from` **[number][428]?** part: its first line, of `linesOfText`
- `to` **[number][428]?** part: its end, exclusive
- `part` **[number][428]?** part, and a gather in parts: which, from 1
- `parts` **[number][428]?** How many parts there are
- `pieces` **[Array][431]<[Piece][48]>?** gather: what it reads
- `answers` **Record<[string][429], [string][429]>** What it describes, by id, with
  what each digest is made from. Empty for a part, whose answer only goes
  into what is put together from it.
- `drop` **[Array][431]<[string][429]>?** Short documents whose old digests go: they are
  read as part of their folder's now
- `sections` **Record<[string][429], [Array][431]<[string][429]>>?** read and part: the long
  sections whose headings it reads, by link, by the document's id: each is
  asked for a line
- `sectionsFrom` **[Array][431]<[string][429]>?** gather of a document read in parts:
  the parts whose answers hold its sections' lines

## ExplorePlan

What an explore job is planned from.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `rootId` **[string][429]** What was explored: a folder, a document, or the
  project's root
- `budget` **[number][428]** How much text a request carries, in characters
- `work` **Record<[string][429], [ExploreWork][49]>** By step id

## PlannedExplore

A plan, and what it will cost.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `plan` **[ExplorePlan][51]**&#x20;
- `steps` **[Array][431]\<JobStep>**&#x20;
- `documents` **[number][428]** How many documents it reads
- `chars` **[number][428]** About how much text it sends, in all

## ExploreReader

What a step reads, as the project is when it runs.

Type: [Object][430]

## SECTIONS_MOST

The most sections of one document that get a line: the longest first.

Type: [number][428]

## SHORT_WORDS

A document shorter than this has no digest of its own: its text is about as
short as one would be, and it is read in its folder's. A note of a hundred
words is worth a line of its own in the listing; a standup of forty is not.

Type: [number][428]

## PACK_MOST

How many documents one request describes at most, when several go together.

## jobs

The long jobs a model does, and how to start one. A job
belongs to a project, its document's, but runs whichever project is open:
the jobs toast lists them all.

- **runner** - Steps run in order, or side by side where they say what they
  wait on; stoppable and resumable
- **sections** - A document's section tree, decided before it is converted
- **convert** - A document's text turned into Markdown, a section at a time
- **explore** - A folder, a document or the whole project described for the
  model, a digest each: in the background, or while a chat waits, on the
  model the chat runs on

A job is a row in the `jobs` table (`stores/jobsStore.js`) with a plan of
steps; the runner walks it, and a kind registered here says what a step
does and what happens at the end. A conversion runs on its workflow's model
(Settings › Workflows); an exploration on the model it keeps, the chat's.
`useJobs` is the composable the outline and the jobs toast use.

## jobs/runner

Running a job: step after step, stoppable, resumable.

A job is a plan of steps and a kind that knows how to run one and what to
do when all are done. The runner starts each step once the steps it waits
on are done, the one before it unless it says otherwise, as many at once
as the connection of its model takes (`ai/gate.js`); it writes each result
as it lands, and stops when told: a pause aborts the requests in flight
and leaves their steps to be done again, a cancel does the same and closes
the job. A step that fails starts no more, and lets those asking finish.
Resuming is starting again; the finished steps are skipped. Nothing here
knows what a step does.

A job runs on the model it keeps (`runsOn`), the one the chat that asked
for it runs on, or else on its workflow's: a kind of job the writer can put
on a model of its own in Settings › Workflows, and which runs on the active
preset until they do.

One job runs at a time per browser tab. The requests it makes are its
own — see `ai/complete.js` — so a chat can go on beside it. A job writes
into its project as it goes, so while it runs the project is its window's
(`platform/windows.js`): no other window opens it until the job stops.

## jobs/sections

A document's sections, decided before any of it is converted.

A conversion that finds structure a chunk at a time finds a different one
in every chunk. Here the whole tree is settled first — from the PDF's own
bookmarks where it has them, and otherwise by one request that reads the
whole text and names its headings — and the text is then cut along it:
each request is a section, or a run of small ones, with its headings
already written in as Markdown. The model converts what is under them;
the structure is not its to choose.

Everything here is pure. The text arrives as lines — a PDF's with the size
each is set in and the page it is on, a text document's with neither.

## SourceLine

A line of the source, where it came from.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `text` **[string][429]** '' for a paragraph break
- `page` **([number][428] | null)** Counted from one; null for a text without pages
- `size` **[number][428]** The size it is set in; 0 when unknown
- `y` **[number][428]?** Its height on the page, for placing a bookmark that names no line
- `bold` **[boolean][432]?** Set in a bold face throughout

## PlannedHeading

A heading of the tree, placed on the source.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `title` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `level` **[number][428]** 1 to 6
- `line` **[number][428]** The line it starts at: its own printed line, or
  the line it is placed before when the source does not print it
- `consumed` **[number][428]** How many source lines are the printed
  heading, and so are not body text; 0 when it is not printed

## Unit

A stretch of the source that is converted as one: a section's body, or
part of one too long for a request.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `heading` **([number][428] | null)** Index into the headings; null for what comes before the first
- `from` **[number][428]** First body line
- `to` **[number][428]** Exclusive
- `part` **[number][428]** 0 for the part that opens with the heading

## Request

What one request converts.

Type: [Object][430]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][429]**&#x20;
- `units` **[Array][431]<[Unit][318]>**&#x20;

## REQUEST_CHARS

How much source one request carries, in characters: about six thousand
tokens of English, which comes back as about as many.

Type: [number][428]

## STRUCTURE_CHARS

How much text the structure request reads whole; past it, only the lines that could be headings.

Type: [number][428]

## DEEPEST

The deepest a heading goes in Markdown.

Type: [number][428]

## NUMBER

A number a heading is printed with: `4.1.6`, `IV`, `Chapter 4`, `Part II`.

## numbered

A bookmark's title with the number its heading is printed with, when the
page gives one and the bookmark leaves it out — `Chapter 4: Early Results`,
`4.1.6 Sampling` — so a reader asking for chapter 4 or section 4.1.6 finds
it by name.

### Parameters

- `title` **[string][429]** The bookmark's
- `above` **([string][429] | null)** A label line printed above the heading
- `printed` **[string][429]** The heading's own printed line

## numbered

Type: [Array][431]<[string][429]>

## LABEL

A line that labels the heading after it: `Chapter 4`, `Part II`, `4`.

## placeBookmarks

Place the PDF's bookmarks on its lines.

Each bookmark is looked for on the page it points at, and the page after,
from where the one before it was placed onward — and failing that,
earlier on its page, since an outline can list a heading after ones the
page prints below it: the printed line that is its heading, or the
lines, when the heading wraps. A label line just above — `Chapter 4` over
the chapter's title — goes with it. The headings come back in the order
the text has them.

A bookmark whose heading is not printed there is written in without
taking a line from the text. One that groups the bookmarks after it —
`Core` over `Dwarf` and `Elf`, pointing at a table on the page before —
goes just before its first child, which is where its section starts. Any
other goes at the height on the page it points to, kept between its
neighbours.

### Parameters

- `lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;
- `outline` &#x20;

Returns **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>**&#x20;

## runningLines

The lines that are running headers and footers: the same text, page
numbers aside, at the same height in the top or bottom tenth of the page
with nothing further out, on a fifth of the pages — or on three pages
running, when it carries a page number. A page number alone is one of them.
What a book repeats in its margins is furniture, not text; left in, it
breaks a table that runs over a page and reads as a heading.

### Parameters

- `lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;
- `heights` **[Map][433]<[number][428], [number][428]>** Each page's height, by page number

Returns **[Set][437]<[number][428]>** The lines' indices

## styleHeadings

The headings a page's type makes, below and between the ones the
bookmarks name: a line set larger than the body, short, and followed by
smaller text — a spell's name over its description, a monster's over its
stat block. Two such lines of one size in a row, the second followed by
smaller text, are one heading set over two lines; three or more are a
table's header, not a heading.

Each takes its level from where it sits: one below the nearest heading
before it that is set larger — a bookmark or another of these — so every
spell under `Spell Descriptions` is one level below it, whichever part of
the book it is in — and never out of the section of the bookmark it is in. Nothing before the first bookmark counts, when there
are bookmarks: that is the title page.

### Parameters

- `lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;
- `marked` **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>** The headings already placed, from bookmarks

Returns **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>** Every heading, the marked ones and these, in text order

## structureOfLayout

A PDF's lines and its section tree, as far as the file itself decides it:
the running headers and footers taken out, the bookmarks placed, and the
headings the type makes below them. Null headings when the PDF has no
bookmarks, for a model to find them instead.

### Parameters

- `layout` &#x20;

## structureMessages

The messages that ask a model for a text's headings. Every line goes with
its number, and — for a PDF — a line set larger than the body carries its
size, which is the strongest sign of a heading there is. A text past the
budget sends only the lines that could be headings: short ones, set large
or standing alone.

### Parameters

- `args` **[Object][430]**&#x20;
  - `args.title` **[string][429]**&#x20;
  - `args.lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][431]<{role: [string][429], content: [string][429]}>**&#x20;

## parseStructure

The headings a structure answer names, checked against the lines: each
on a line that exists, in order, at a level from 1 to 6. A heading that
wraps takes the lines its title runs over.

### Parameters

- `answer` **[string][429]** One heading per line: `<line> <level> <title>`
- `lines` **[Array][431]<[SourceLine][314]>**&#x20;

<!---->

- Throws **[Error][435]** When the answer names no headings the lines have

Returns **[Array][431]<[PlannedHeading][316]>**&#x20;
